limitations: Boundary uses CPU quota only; recovery helper fixes cpuset 0,1.
Transient memory.stat anon/file can lag /proc RssAnon/RssFile. Stage points are observations, not allocation census; retained continuous samples and RSS corroborate large steady-state conclusions.
memory.peak reaching memory.max with max events and page-cache reclaim is not an OOM or a leak.
Raw io.stat on shared backing device is uncalibrated; no physical IO attribution, write amplification, or official resource score is claimed.
Successful 2m is the tested ceiling, not proof of the maximum supported cardinality. Baseline first tested failure was 2m; exact threshold was not searched.
Single-run boundary/transaction/retention wall times are diagnostics, not paired performance estimates.
Independent recovery helper compiles only frozen storage implementation with -O3 -DNDEBUG. Its constructor clock is not production process end-to-end performance.
Recovery fixture copies and hash verification prepopulate the host file cache; these are process-cold, not OS-cold tests.

Recovery constructor row verification counts all rows/lengths and checks independent expected bytes at sampled keys; noncryptographic cross-version FNV is corroboration rather than an independent complete oracle.
